Council, hereby makes the following Ordinances, namely:

commencement.- Ordinances, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the

2. Definitions.- (1) In these Ordinances, unless the context otherwise requires— 
(a) “academic council” means the Academic Council of the 
University; 


(b) “academic staff’ means such categories of staff as are designated 
as academic staff by these Ordinances; 

(०) “Act” means Central Universities Act 2009 (25 of 2009); 

(d) “affiliation and recognition board” means Affiliation and 
Recognition Board of the University; 

(e) “Board of studies” means the Board of Studies of the University; 

(f) “Campus” means the unit established or constituted by the 
University for making arrangements for instruction, research, 
education and training; 

(g) “finance officer” means the Finance Officer of the University; 

(h) “hostels” means hostels of the University; 

(i) “institution” means an institution, school, college or centre of 
studies maintained by or admitted to the privileges of the 
University for imparting education and training in its disciplines; 

(0) “professor of practice”, “chair professor’, “joint faculty”, 
“adjunct faculty”, “distinguished faculty”, “honorary professor” 
and visiting faculty” means the faculty appointed in accordance 
with the guidelines framed by the Executive Council; 

(k) “seniority list” means the list on seniority of any employee, 
maintained by the University; 

(0) “University” means Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya established 
under Section 3F of the Central Universities Act, 2009 (25 of 
2009); 


(2) The words and expressions used in these ordinances and not defined, 
but defined in the act and statues, shall have the same meaning espectively 
aligned to them in the Act and Statutes. 


(3) Should there be any difference in interpretation of these Ordinances 
amongst the English and Hindi versions due to translation error, the

३... Application.- The Ordinances may provide for all or any of the following matters, 
namely: — 
(1) the admission of students to the University and their enrolment 
as such; 
(2) the courses of study to be laid down for all degrees, diplomas 
and certificates of the University; 
(3) the medium of instruction and examination; 


(4) the award of degrees, diplomas, certificates and other academic 
distinctions, the qualifications for the same and the means to be 
taken relating to the granting and obtaining of the same; 

(5) the fees to be charged for courses of study in the University and 
for admission to examinations, degrees and diplomas to the 
University; 

(6) the conditions for award of fellowships, scholarships, 
studentships, medals and prizes; 

(7) the conduct of examination, including the term of office and 
manner of appointment and the duties of examining bodies, 
examiners and moderators; 

(8) the conditions of residence of the students of the University; 


(9) the special arrangements, if any, which may be made for the 
residence and teaching of women students and the prescribing of 
special courses of studies for them; 

(10) the establishment of Centres of Studies, Boards of Studies, 
Specialised Laboratories and other Committees; 

(11) the manner of co-operation and collaboration with other 
Universities, Institutions and other agencies including learned 
bodies or associations; 

(12) the creation, composition and functions of any other body which 
is considered necessary for improving the academic life of the 
University; 

(13) the institution of fellowships, scholarships, studentships, medals 
and prizes; 

(14) the setting up of machinery for redressal of grievances of 
employees and students; and 

(15) all other matters which by this Act, or, the Statutes, are to be, or 
may be provided for by the Ordinances.

(a) The Vice-Chancellor shall be the principal executive and 
academic officer of the University and shall exercise general 
supervision and control over the affairs of the University and 
give effect to the decisions of all the authorities of the 
University; 

(b) The Vice-Chancellor, if he is of the opinion that any decision of 
any authority of the University is beyond the powers of the 
authority conferred by the provisions of the Act, the Statutes or 
the Ordinances of the University or that any decision taken is not 
in the interest of the University, may ask the authority concerned 
to review its decision within sixty days of such decision and if 
the authority refuses to review the decision either in whole or in 
part or no decision is taken by it within the said period of sixty 
days, the matter shall be referred to the Visitor whose decision 
thereon shall be final; 

(c) The Vice-Chancellor shall not act upon any decision of any 
authority, if he is of the opinion that: 

(i) 1115 ultra vires of the provisions of the Act, the Statutes, 
or the Ordinances of the University; 

(ii) such a decision shall not be in the best interests of the 
University. In either case, he may ask the authority 
concerned to review the decision, and if any difference 
persists, the matter shall be referred to the Visitor, whose 
decision shall be final; 

(d) As the Chairman of any authority, body or committee of the 
University, he shall be empowered to suspend a member from 
the meeting of the authority, body or committee for obstructing 
or stalling the proceedings or for indulging in behavior 
unbecoming of a member of such Committee; 

(e) The Vice-Chancellor shall have disciplinary powers with regard 
to employees of the University; 

(f) In an emergent situation, he shall take any action on behalf of 
any authority in which the power is vested and to report the 
action taken in the next meeting of the authority; 

(g) He shall be empowered to allocate responsibilities and to audit 
the performance of officers, faculty members and staff against 
the expected standards; 

(h) He shall exercise all administrative and financial powers 
considered necessary for smooth and efficient functioning of the 
University; 

(i) He shall pass such orders and take such measures that are 
necessary to implement any of the above powers and duties; 

(Gj) He shall be empowered to appoint or engage members of 
teaching and non-teaching employees possessing necessary 
qualifications for a period not exceeding one year to meet the 
urgent requirement of the University; 

(k) The Vice-Chancellor may delegate such powers and duties for 
day-to-day work to such person as deemed fit.

limit of three hundred days;

appointed on probation for a period of twelve months which may 
be extended by the Executive Council wherever necessary. 

Provided that the case of each teacher shall be considered 

for confirmation by a duly constituted review committee or by 
the Vice-Chancellor and shall be reported to the Executive 
Council closer to the conclusion of the probation period and the 
teacher shall be informed of the decision not later than fifteen 
days prior to the expiration of the period of probation. 
(b) Where a teacher appointed on probation is found, during the 
period of probation, not suitable for holding that post or has not 
completed the period of probation whether extended or not, 
satisfactorily, the Executive Council may (i) if the appointment 
is by promotion, revert the incumbent to the previous post held 
by him; and (ii) if the appointment is by direct recruitment, 
terminate the teacher’s services under the University without 
notice. 

(6) Increment: Every teacher shall be entitled to draw his increment 
in his scale of pay unless it is withheld or postponed by a 
resolution of the Executive Council on a reference by the Vice- 
Chancellor and the teacher has been provided with an adequate 
opportunity of making his representation as to why such an 
action shall not be taken. 

(7) Leave: Every teacher shall be eligible for leave as stated in 
Ordinance-35 (Leave rules of Teaching Faculty). 

(8) Retirement: All teachers shall retire at the end of the month in 
which they complete the age of sixty-five years; 

Provided that the University may permit the teacher to 
continue to serve after retirement as aforesaid till the end of the 
academic year to ensure that the teaching work is not dislocated. 

(9) Re-employment of retired persons as teachers and part-time 
teachers: Notwithstanding the provisions of clause (8) above, the 
University may engage any person who has superannuated on 
contract to serve the University in teaching and other academic 
activities subject to such guidelines as the Executive Council 
may from time to time issue in this regard and that pay shall be 
fixed according to the Government of India instructions on the 
pay fixation of pensioners; 

Provided that no person who has attained the age of 
seventy years be appointed under this clause.

Council engage directly or indirectly in any employment, trade 
or business to which any emolument or honorarium or other

or literary or scientific work or publication or radio talk or 
extension lecturers or other academic work undertaken with the

the time being in force as well as a code of professional ethics as

result in a continuous absence from duty during the entire period,

(ii) if a person in the permanent service of the University is 
appointed ‘on probation’ to a higher post, during probation, he 
shall not be deprived of the benefit of leave rules applicable to 
his permanent post; 


(p) Teacher Appointed on Contract Basis: 


Teachers appointed on contract basis shall be entitled to leave as 
under: 

(i) earned leave or half pay leave or casual leave as admissible 
to whole time temporary teachers of the University; 

(ii) in the case of contract appointments for one year of less, 
unless on medical grounds, no extraordinary leave shall be 
granted; 

(ili) in the case of contract appointments for more than one year 
but less than five years, extraordinary leave as admissible to 
temporary teachers’ subject to the condition that the total period 
of extraordinary leave during the entire contract period shall not 
exceed ninety days; 

(iv) where the contract appointment is for five years or more, the 
extraordinary leave shall be as that admissible to the whole time 
temporary teachers; 


(q) General Conditions Applicable to All Categories of Teachers: 


(i) Right to leave: 

(a) No leave shall be claimed as matter of right, leave of any 
kind may be varied, refused or revoked by the competent 
authority empowered to grant it without assigning any 
reason, if that authority considers such action to be in the 
interest of the University; 

(b) No leave shall be granted to a teacher whom a 
competent authority has decided to dismiss, remove or 
compulsorily retire from service, nor shall any leave be 
granted to a teacher who is under suspension;

(vii)Re-joining duty on return from leave on medical

(xx) Cash Payment In lieu of Leave: 


(a) On Superannuation.- 

Where a teacher superannuates on attaining the normal age 
prescribed for superannuation under the terms and 
conditions governing his service, the authority competent to 
grant leave shall suo motu authorise encashment of earned 
leave, if any, at the credit of the teacher on the date of his 
superannuation, subject to a maximum of three hundred 
days and this limit shall be as applicable to Government of 
India employees; 

(b) Superannuation while under suspension.- 

A teacher, who superannuates while under suspension, shall 
become eligible for the benefit of cash equivalent of earned 
leave at his credit on the date of his superannuation on 
conclusion of the proceedings against him, if the competent 
authority decides to re-instate him in service and holds that 
the suspension was wholly unjustified; 

(c) Retirement before superannuation.- 

A teacher who retires or is retired from service may be 
granted suo moto, by the authority competent to grant leave, 
cash equivalent of leave salary in respect of earned leave at 
his credit subject to maximum number of days including 
days in respect of the half pay leave at his credit as specified 
by the Government of India or regulatory authorities from 
time to time; 

Provided that this period does not exceed the 
period between the date on which he so retires or is retired 
from service and the date on which he shall have retired in 
the normal course after attaining the age prescribed for 
superannuation under the terms and conditions governing 
his service, the cash equivalent shall be equal to the leave 
salary as admissible for earned leave and equal to the leave 
salary as admissible for half pay leave plus dearness 
allowance admissible on that leave salary for the first three 
hundred days, at the rates in force on the date the University 
employee so retires or is retired from service, the pension 
and pension equivalent of other retirement benefits and ad 
hoc relief or graded relief on pension shall be deducted from 
the leave salary paid for the period of half pay leave, if any, 
for which the cash equivalent is payable and this limit shall 
stand revised as per Government of India orders issued from 
time to time; 

Settlement or no house rent allowance shall be payable; 

Provided that if leave salary for the half pay 
leave component falls short of pension and other pensionary 
benefits, cash equivalent of half pay leave shall not be 
granted:

(i) resignation: if a teacher (confirmed employee)

shall stand revised as per Government of India orders 
issued from time to time; 

(e) Dismissal or Removal.- 
When a teacher is dismissed or removed from service 
following disciplinary proceedings he shall not be 
eligible for leave encashment.

(1i)the cash equivalent thus payable shall be equal to the

issued from time to time; 

(g) Leave encashment of a teacher who dies while in 

harness.- 

In case a teacher dies in harness, the cash equivalent of the 

leave salary that the deceased teacher shall have got, had he 

gone on earned leave, but for the death, due and admissible 

on the date immediately following the date of death subject 

to a maximum of leave salary for three hundred days shall 

be paid to his family and this limit shall stand revised as per 

Government of India orders issued from time to time; 

(h) Calculation of cash equivalent of leave.- 

The cash equivalent of leave shall be calculated and payable 

in one lump sum as a one-time settlement as per 

Government of India rules;

The Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, by nature, is a Central University, a 
pioneer in the domain of transport and logistics education in India and 
the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya promotes excellence in quality and 
prefers to maintain good quality professionals in the faculty cadre. 
The cadre structure is different from Indian Institutes of Technology 
cadre structure but in quality, there is no compromise. Since, the 
Assistant Professor level induction is at academic level-10 in the pay 
matrix (Rs.57700-182400), Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya has to 
provide promotional avenues so as to keep the faculty motivated and 
avoid attrition. As Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya is recruiting faculty 
who are pass-outs from Indian Institutes of Technology or Indian 
Institutes of Management or the premier National Institutes of 
Technology, meritocracy shall prevail in promotion and not the time- 
bound or in-situ promotion. Such a policy shall motivate the 
performers. 


(1) Career Progression at Assistant Professor Level: The 
movement from level-10 to level-11 and level-11 to level-12 in 
the pay matrix of the 7” Central Pay Commission shall be 
through selection and not in-situ. 

(2) The selection committee shall have at least one external member 
in the level of Professor or above and this scheme shall be 
termed career progression for faculty. 

(3) The minimum residency period at Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya 
for movement of faculty from Academic pay level-10 to 
Academic pay level-11 shall be one year and on successful 
completion of probation period; and for movement from 
Academic pay level-11 to Academic pay level-12, two years 
from the date of joining on Academic pay level-11. 

(4) Movement to the level of Associate Professor and Professor shall 
only be through selection, after the required residency as in 
Indian Institutes of Technology. 

(5) For the position of Associate Professor, the candidate shall have 
at least a minimum of six years (post Doctor of Philosophy) 
teaching, research or industrial experience out of which at least 
three years shall be at the level of Assistant Professor in 
academic level-12 in the pay matrix (Rs. 79800-211500) in a 
reputed Institute or University or equivalent. 

(6) For the position of Professor, at least a minimum of ten years 
(post Doctor of Philosophy) teaching, research or industrial

experience out of which at least four years shall be at the level of 
Associate Professor or at an equivalent level.

are accurate and in proper order in all cases and a certificate to 
this effect duly signed by the officer designated for the purpose 
shall form a part of the note for the Departmental Promotion 
Committee; 

(c) Penalties of any kind (major) shall constitute a bar to one's 
eligibility for promotion or confirmation as per Department of 
Personnel and Training guidelines, however, minor penalty of 
"censure" shall not constitute a bar on the eligibility and

unless otherwise mentioned specifically in the order about such a

The following cases shall be brought to the notice of the 

Departmental Promotion Committee: 

(i) employees under suspension; 

(ii) in respect of whom a charge-sheet has been issued and 
disciplinary proceedings are pending; and 

(iii) in respect of whom prosecution for a criminal charge has 
been pending in the Court of Law; 


Note : The Departmental Promotion Committee shall assess their 
suitability without regard to the disciplinary aspect, the findings 
of the Departmental Promotion Committee shall be kept in a 
sealed cover as per the fact recorded in the proceedings of the 
Departmental Promotion Committee, the same procedures shall 
be followed by subsequent Departmental Promotion Committee 
till the disciplinary or criminal cases are concluded. On 
conclusion of the case, the sealed cover shall be opened. In case 
the officer is completely exonerated, the due date of his 
promotion shall be determined and he shall be promoted 
notionally with reference to the date of promotion of his junior 
and if necessary by reverting the junior most officiating person, 
if not exonerated, the recommendations of the Departmental 
Promotion Committee in sealed cover shall not be acted upon; 

(d) The cases of officers under cloud after clearance by the 
Departmental Promotion Committee shall be settled in 
accordance with the Government of India rules. 


(25) Functions of the Departmental Promotion Committee: 

(a) The Departmental Promotion Committee shall consider and 
make recommendations in all cases of Group ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’ 
employees and the constitution of Departmental Promotion 
Committee (DPC) for various categories of posts shall be as 
prescribed under the Cadre Recruitment Rules of the University. 

(b) While considering the promotional cases, the Departmental 
Promotion Committee shall consider the followings namely:- 

(i) provisions of the rules or Act or Statutes or Ordinances or 
University Regulations or regulatory authority Regulations 
or Guidelines and Government of India rules as applicable 
from time to time; 


244 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(ii) eligibility criteria and relaxations or concessions 
applicable to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes 
or the Persons with Benchmark Disabilities categories; 

(ii) work and conduct reports; 

(iv) the Annual Performance Appraisal Reports for the 
preceding five years along with the Annual Property 
Returns as available with the Competent Authority, while 
screening the Annual Performance Appraisal Reports, the 
Departmental Promotion Committee may also adopt the 
criteria with regard to the bench marks as mentioned in the 
Statutes or Ordinances or Government of India rules; 

(v) vigilance clearance report; 

(vi) roster points of the cadres as per the reservation policy of 
the Government of India; 

(vii) performance in the interview or skill test or written test, if 
conducted by the University as per rules; 

(viii) the Departmental Promotion Committee is expected to 
screen the cases and decide the eligibility based on the 
aforementioned documents like Annual Performance 
Appraisal Reports, Vigilance Clearance Report, Roster, 
Recruitment Rules, etc. 


Note: In case Annual Performance Appraisal Reports for any 
particular period has not been written or endorsed by the 
designated authority despite the fact that the employee 
concerned produces the proof of submission of self-appraisal 
report(s) duly filled-in for that particular period(s) to the 
concerned section, the Departmental Promotion Committee or 
Screening Committee shall ignore the report(s) of that particular 
period(s) and shall take into account the report(s) of the 
immediately preceding period(s). It is mandatory on the part of 
the designated officer to make entry in the relevant register to be 
maintained for this purpose and issue proper receipt to the 
employee concerned as a proof of submission of the appraisal 
reports. There shall be proper entry in the relevant register with 
regard to each movement of the Annual Performance Appraisal 
Report till the completion of its process. 


(26) Mode of promotion: 


(a) The university shall strictly adhere to the quota prescribed for 
promotion of the eligible internal candidates as per the 
recruitment rules, in case candidates are not available under the 
internal quota and the posts are filled up through direct 
recruitment in the interest of the university, future vacancy may 
be shifted proportionately to the promotion quota and filled up 
out of the eligible internal candidates from the feeder cadre, in 
the light of the above, the Departmental Promotion Committee 
(DPC) shall be required to ensure the number of available 
vacancies under the promotion quota; 

(b) In addition to the above conditions for promotion for the posts, 
University may decide the method and procedure to be followed 
for promotion in respect of any category of posts, for this 


[भाग [खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र असाधारण : 245 


purpose, the University, at its discretion, may opt the fitness- 
cum-seniority or hold written test or other trade or professional 
tests and fix qualifying marks for any post to assess the 
competence in an objective manner. In such cases, association of 
at least one external expert shall be mandatory; 

(c) Mere possession of eligibility conditions shall not entitle an 
employee to be promoted to the next higher post from the date of 
his eligibility, after completion of formalities such as Annual 
Performance Appraisal Reports or Annual Confidential Reports, 
Vigilance Clearance Report, the Departmental Promotion 
Committee may be constituted to evaluate and assess the 
eligibility of the employees, the employees shall be considered 
for promotion based on the recommendations of the 
Departmental Promotion Committee duly approved by the 
Competent Authority of the University; 

(d) All promotions of the non-teaching staff belonging to Group ‘A’, 
‘B’ and Group ‘C’ shall take effect from the date of joining; 

(e) Qualifying in typing test or skill test with knowledge of 
computers shall be the compulsory requirement for promotion to 
the post of Assistant, Superintendent, Library Assistant and other 
positions as identified from time to time. Further, qualifying in 
typing test or skill test with knowledge of computers shall be the 
compulsory requirement for all Assistants or Superintendents of 
the University as per the eligibility criteria prescribed in these 
rules as prescribed for direct recruitment. The University may 
impose any condition to be complied with at a future date failing 
which, the Competent Authority may order for stoppage of 
increment. 


(27) Ad-hoc promotions: 

In case there is an existing vacancy and no eligible employee is 
available in the feeder Cadre for promotion, the Competent 
Authority may consider relaxation by a maximum period of one 
year at its discretion to promote an employee on ad-hoc basis 
after completing all procedural formalities, as laid down under 
rule 24 above, however, this arrangement shall not be allowed to 
continue beyond one year in case the employee concerned is not 
considered for regular promotion. 


(28) Panel: 
The panel drawn for promotion or direct recruitment shall be 
valid for a period of one year from the date of the meeting of the 
Departmental Promotion Committee date of approval of the 
recommendations, respectively. 


(29) Career Advancement Scheme: 
The Career Advancement Scheme for the non-teaching staff shall 
be decided by the Executive Council. 

30) Deputation: 

(a) The University may fill up any post on deputation by drawing 
officers from Government of India or autonomous bodies or 
public sector undertakings as per University Grants Commission 
or Government of India rules, the officer to be considered for 
deputation against any post below pay level-14 in the pay matrix 


246 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(Rs. 144200-218200) must be less than fifty-six years of age and 
Pay level -14 and above must be less than fifty-eight years of 
age, in case the appointment is made on deputation by following 
the due process of selection prescribed for the post under the 
cadre recruitment rules, the incumbent may be allowed to 
continue for the period as prescribed by the Government of India 
from time to time or till he attains the age of superannuation 
prescribed for that particular cadre, whichever is earlier; 


(b) An appointment on deputation may be made initially for a period 
of three years (except statutory posts) which may be extended 
further at the discretion of the Competent Authority subject to 
satisfactory performance; 


(c) The University, however, shall have the right to repatriate all 
incumbents, including the incumbents holding the statutory 
posts, at any time even before the prescribed period in case his 
performance, integrity or conduct are found to be unsatisfactory 
at any stage, in the opinion of the Competent Authority; 


(d) Ordinarily, no person working on deputation shall be absorbed in 
any post of the University after expiry of his period of 
deputation, in case, it is decided in the interest of the University 
to absorb any such person, then the University may take up the 
matter with his parent organisation for concurrence after 
obtaining the option of the employee concerned subject to the 
condition that the matter of absorption is specifically mentioned 
in the advertisement, after obtaining the consent of the parent 
department, the case shall be placed before the Competent 
Authority for a final decision if he is absorbed in the University, 
he shall be assigned the bottom seniority of that particular cadre 
as per the Government of India rules. 


(31) Probation: 

(a) (i) In case of direct recruitment, the selected candidate shall be 
kept on probation for a period as specified in these rules, the date 
from which confirmation shall be given effect is the date 
following the date of satisfactory completion of the prescribed 
period of probation or the extended period of probation, as the 
case may be, the decision to confirm the probationer or to extend 
the period of probation as the case may be shall be 
communicated to the probationer normally within six to eight 
weeks prior to the completion of probation period; 

(ii) Probation shall not be extended for more than a year and, in 
no circumstances, an employee shall be kept on probation for 
more than double the normal prescribed period of probation, the 
officer shall be deemed to have successfully completed the 
probation period if no order confirming, discharging or reverting 
the officer is issued within eight weeks after expiry of double the 
normal period of prescribed probation, on completion of the 
probation period or any extension thereof, employees shall, if 
considered fit for permanent appointment, be retained in the 
appointments on regular basis and be confirmed against the 
available substantive vacancies as the case may be; 

(iii) In case there is no perceivable improvement despite all this,

his services shall be discharged by giving him one month's 
notice in advance or on payment of one month's salary in lieu of 
notice., the employee concerned may also exercise his option to 
resign by giving one month's notice; 

(b) As regards other matters relating to probation, the employee shall 
be governed by the instructions issued by the Government of 
India in this regard from time to time; 

(c) In the case of promotion to the next higher group, the 
employee(s) shall be kept on probation for a period of two years 
from the date of joining, the Appointing Authority may at its 
discretion, extend the period of probation by one year on ground 
of non-performance, misconduct or misbehavior or if he fails to 
comply with the terms and conditions of the appointment to the 
post to which he was promoted, in case there is no perceivable 
improvement despite all this, he shall be reverted to his parent 
post, with immediate effect, and consequently all the employees 
promoted against the consequential vacancies due to the 
promotion of this employee shall be reverted to their respective 
parent posts, in case they shall not be adjusted in any other 
similar vacant posts, however, there shall not be any probation 
for promotion within the same group. 


Note: 

(i) if an employee who has been recruited or promoted to any 
post, avail himself of leave on a piecemeal basis, or at a 
time for a period of two months or more during the period of 
probation, his probation shall be extended proportionately, 
i.e., equal to the total period of leave availed by the 
employee concerned; 

(ii) In order to avoid any anomalous situation, all cases of 
probation of the officials shall be reviewed in every six 
months, in case, the result of review of performance of an 
official is found to be unsatisfactory, or not up to the mark, he 
shall be apprised of the consequences of unsatisfactory 
performance during the period of probation and such an 
appraisal shall be issued in advance after which the 
performance of the official concerned shall be continuously 
kept under observation; 

(iii) notwithstanding anything contained in the above-mentioned 
provision, if a probationer is placed under suspension 
during the period of probation, the period of probation may 
be extended till such period as the Appointing Authority 
deems fit in the circumstances; 

(iv) as for temporary Government servants they shall, as a 
matter of rule, be asked to resign from the parent 
department or office at the time of release from the parent 
department or office, an undertaking to the effect that he 
shall resign from the parent department or office, in the 
event of his selection and appointment to the post applied 
for, may be taken from his at the time of forwarding the 
application, this procedure is to be followed even in case of 
a temporary Government servant applying as a direct

(v) an employee of the University shall be confirmed through 
Departmental Confirmation Committee (or a committee 
constituted for the purpose by the Vice Chancellor); 

(vi) an employee of the University shall not be confirmed on his 
post unless and until he signs the ‘Service Agreement’; 

(vit) there shall be no probation in the case of an employee 
appointed to a post on deputation, tenure or on re- 
employment after superannuation; and 

(viii) the Appointing Authority shall record the reasons in writing 
while terminating the appointment of a probationer or 
extension of the normal period of probation.

Authority Regulations: 

(a) If any particular provision concerning the qualifications for

silent, the corresponding rules operating in the Government of

mutatis mutandis; 

(b) the pay matrix contained in the schedules for various posts shall 
be revised as per the government or regulatory authority

(34) Disqualification: The following categories of persons shall not be 
eligible to apply for any position in the University, namely: - 

(a) who has been convicted by any Court of Law or any criminal

(e) any other category of person disqualified for appointment by the

Commission from time to time. 


(35) Vigilance clearance: 

(a) Candidate who is already in service shall submit the Vigilance 
Clearance Certificate from the employer or his authorised 
officer, to the effect that no disciplinary or criminal proceedings 
are pending or contemplated against him, it shall be directly sent 
by the parent department or be handed over to the employee 
concerned in sealed cover at the time of written or skill test 
or interview as applicable or along with the application. 

(b) (७) Willful suppression of factual information or any document

(36) Removal of difficulties: If any difficulty arises in _ the 
implementation or operation of any of the provision of these 
rules, the Vice-Chancellor may, from time to time issue with the 
approval of the Executive Council, such general or specific 
directions but not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, 
Statutes, Ordinances or directives of the Government of India, 
Ministry of Education or University Grants Commission, which 
appear to be necessary for the purpose of removing such 
difficulty. 


(37) Interpretation: Any ambiguity or lack of clarity with regard to 
any clause of the rules, the matter may be referred to the 
Executive Council of the University for clarification. 


(38) Amendment of rules: Any amendment, modification, changes, 
withdrawal, suspension and relaxation in any or all of 
provisions of these rules shall be done with prior approval 
of Government of India,- 

(a) the matters not specified or referred to in these rules, the 
corresponding provisions as provided by the Government of 
India relating to its employees, shall be followed, in case any 
particular provision in these rules is in conflict with any 
provision of the regulatory body or Government of India Orders, 
the provisions of regulatory body or Government of India Orders 
shall prevail; 

(b) The non-teaching employees and other academic staff shall be 
liable to serve anywhere in India within the jurisdiction of the 
University; 

(c) Incase of any dispute, the territorial jurisdiction for adjudication 
shall be the “Vadodara Court”; 

(d) All the existing rules and Orders in relation to the matters 
covered under these rules shall stand repealed but any action 
already taken pursuant to such existing rules and orders shall be 
deemed to have been taken under these rules.

the University 1. (a) These rules may be called the “Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya

PART - II: DEFINITIONS 
3. In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires, 


(1) ‘average pay’ means the average monthly pay earned during the 
10 complete calendar months immediately preceding the month 
in which the event occurs which necessitates the calculation of 
average pay; 

(2) ‘Cadre’ means the strength of a service or a part of a service 
sanctioned as a separate unit; 

(3) ‘Compensatory Allowance’ means an allowance granted to an 
employee to meet the personal expenditure necessitated by the 
special circumstances in which duty is performed, it includes 
traveling allowance. 

(4) ‘duty’ includes (a) service on probation provided that such 
service is followed by confirmation: (b) joining time. An 
employee may be treated as on duty during the course of 
instruction or training. 

(5) ‘employee (non-teaching)’ means a University employee other 
than Teaching Staff; 

(6) ‘fee’ means a recurring or non-recurring payment made to an 
employee from a source other than the funds of the University 
whether made directly to the employee or indirectly through the 
intermediary of the University but it does not include un -earned 
income such as income from property, dividends and interests on 
securities and income from literary, artistic, cultural, scientific 
and technological efforts; 

(7) ‘honorarium’ means a recurring or non-recurring payment 
granted to an employee from the funds of the University as 
remuneration for special work of an occasional or intermittent 
character; 

(8) ‘foreign Service’ means service in which an employee receives 
his pay with the sanction of the University from a source other 
than the funds of the University; 

(9) ‘joining Time’ means the time allowed to an employee to travel 
to or from a station to which he is posted on transfer from one 
station to another within the jurisdiction of the University; 

(10) ‘leave salary’ means the monthly amount paid by the University 


[भाग पा--_खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र असाधारण : 261 


to an employee who is on leave; 

(11) ‘lien’ means the title of an employee to hold substantively either 
immediately, or on the termination of a period or periods of 
absence, a permanent post, including a tenure post, to which he 
has been appointed substantively; 

(12) ‘month’ means a calendar month, in calculating a period 
expressed in terms of months and days, complete calendar 
months, irrespective of the number of days in each, shall first be 
calculated and the odd number of days calculated subsequently; 

(13) ‘officiating’ means an employee officiates in a post when he 
performs the duties of a post on which another employee is 
holding a lien, an employee may also officiate in a vacant post 
on which no other employee holds a lien; 

(14) ‘pay’ means the amount drawn monthly by an employee as: 

(a) The pay other than special pay or pay granted in view of his 
personal qualifications which has been sanctioned for a post 
held by him substantively or in an officiating capacity or to 
which he is entitled by reason of his position in a cadre; and 

(b) Special pay and personal pay; 

(15) ‘personal Pay’ means additional pay granted to an employee- 

(a) to save him from loss of substantive pay in respect of a 
permanent post, other than a tenure post, due to revision of 
pay or to any reduction of such substantive pay, otherwise 
than as a disciplinary measure; or 

(b)in exceptional circumstances on other personal 
considerations; 

(16) ‘probation’ means a person on probation in a post is one 
appointed to that post for determining his fitness for eventual 
substantive appointment to the post; 

(17) ‘Special Pay’ means an addition of the nature of pay, to the 
emoluments of a post or of an employee, granted in 
consideration of. 

(a) The specially arduous nature of the duties; or 

(b) A specific addition to the work or responsibility; 

(18) ‘permanent post’ means a post carrying a definite rate of pay 
sanctioned without limit of time; 

(19) ‘substantive pay’ means the pay other than special pay or 
personal pay to which an employee is entitled to on account of a 
post to which he has been appointed substantively; 

(20) ‘subsistence grant? means monthly grant made to an employee 
who is not in receipt of pay or leave salary; 

(21) ‘temporary post’ means a post carrying a definite rate of pay 
sanctioned for a limited time; 

(22) ‘time scale pay’ means pay which rises by periodical increments 
from a minimum to a maximum; 

(23) ‘travelling allowance’ means an allowance granted to an 
employee to cover the expenses which he incurs in traveling in 
the interests of the University; 

(24) the words and expression used in these rules and defined, but 
defined in the Act, Statutes and Ordinances shall have the same 
meaning respectively, assigned to them in the Act, Statutes and

(2) Qualifications for appointment: The age, qualifications and 
method of recruitment for appointment to various posts in the 
University shall be such as may be prescribed in the relevant 
recruitment rules or as determined by the Executive Council 
from time to time. 

(3) Fitness: 

(a) Appointment of persons by direct recruitment for a period 
for more than three months shall be subject to their being 
found medically fit by the Medical Officer of the University 
or any other Medical Authority authorised for the purpose or 
by a Medical Officer not below the rank of a Civil Surgeon; 

(b) No person shall be appointed to any post unless the 
Appointing Authority is satisfied that he possesses good 
character and conduct. 

(4) Methods of recruitment: - Recruitment to posts may be made- 

(a) By direct recruitment; or 

(b) By promotion; or 

(c) By transfer; or 

(d) By deputation from Government Departments and other 

institutions; 

(e) By deputation followed by absorption. 

(5) Recruitment by Promotion: 

(a) Appointment to a post in any grade by promotion shall be 
made, whether in a permanent or officiating capacity, from 
amongst employees serving in posts in the next lower grade; 

(b) Every appointment by promotion shall be on the basis of 
suitability due regard being paid to seniority. 

(6) Appointment: - 

(a) Appointment to a post shall be made by the Executive 
Council or by the Officer authorised by it for the purpose on 
the recommendations of Selection Committee constituted for 
the purpose from time to time; 

(0) The age, educational and other qualifications for 
appointment to the post and the method of recruitment shall

(7) Adhoc Appointments: - 

Notwithstanding anything contained in the above rule, the 

Executive Council may by a general or special order and subject 

to such conditions as it may specify in such order delegate to any 

authority in the University the power to make ad_ hoc 
appointments. 

(8) Appointments in the place of employees dismissed or removed 

or reduced: 
Where an employee has been dismissed, removed or reduced 
from any cadre in the service, no vacancy caused thereby or 
arising subsequently in such cadre in the service shall be 
substantively filled to the prejudice of such person until the 
appeal, if any, preferred by him against such dismissal, or 
reduction is decided, and except in conformity with such 
decision or until the time allowed for preferring an appeal has 
expired, as the case may be. 

(9) Re-employment in service beyond the date of superannuation: 
Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, the Executive 
Council shall have power: 

(a) to extend the services of the employees of the University 
beyond the age of superannuation; 

(b) to re-employ persons who have worked under the Central 
Government or State Government or Union Territory 
administration or other Universities and who have retired 
from service on superannuation or on other grounds except 
on invalid grounds. 

(c) To absorb permanently Government servants who have been 
on deputation to the University and to retain them on re- 
employment basis. 


Note: The over-riding consideration by the Executive Council for 
the grant of extension of service or re-employment is that it must 
be in the interest of the University and in addition satisfy one of 
the following two conditions: 

(i) that no suitable person shall be made available from the 
lower cadre on promotion or there is shortage in that cadre; 
(ii) that the retiring officer is of outstanding merit: 

Provided that no Officer shall be retained in the 
service of the University beyond two years from the date of 
superannuation prescribed by the University. 

(10) Except as otherwise provided in these rules, the whole time of 
the employee of the University is at the disposal of the University 
which pays him and he may be employed in any manner required 
by proper authority without claim for additional remuneration:- 


(a) The absence of an employee of the University from duty, 
whether on leave or on foreign service shall not render him 
ineligible to the privileges in respect of seniority, promotion 
and confirmation which he shall have enjoyed but for his 
absence if he is fit otherwise; 

(b) No permanent employee shall be granted leave of any kind

for a continuous period exceeding five years; 

(c) When an employee does not resume duty after remaining on 
leave for a continuous period of five years, or where an 
employee after the expiry of his leave remains absent from 
duty, otherwise than on foreign service or on account of 
suspension, or for any period which together with the period 
of leave granted to him exceeds five years, he shall unless 
the Executive Council, in view of the exceptional 
circumstances of the case otherwise determines, be deemed 
to have resigned and shall accordingly cease to be in the 
University service. 


(11) Tenure: 

(a) Every person appointed on regular basis to a post in the 
University whether by promotion or by direct recruitment, 
shall be on probation in that post for a period of two years: 

Provided that the appointing authority may, in 

any individual case, extend the period of probation for a 

further period not exceeding two years the reason thereof to 

be recorded in writing; 

(b) Where a person appointed to a post in the University on 
probation is, during his regular period of probation, or 
extended period of probation found unsuitable for holding 
that post or has not completed his period of probation 
satisfactorily the appointing authority may: 

(i) 11 the case of person appointed by promotion revert 
him to the post held by him immediately before such 
appointment; and 

(ii) in the case of a person appointed by direct recruitment 
terminate his services under the University without 
notice; 

(c) Every person appointed to a permanent post under the 
University by promotion or by direct recruitment shall, on 
satisfactory completion of his period of probation be eligible 
for confirmation in that post, confirmation shall be through a 
committee appointed by the Vice-Chancellor to review the 
performance during probation; 

(d) No employee shall be confirmed in any post unless the 
service of the employee under the University is approved by 
the Appointing Authority; 

(e) The seniority of an employee regularly appointed to a post 
according to rule shall be determined by the order of merit

50... Anti-plagiarism policy.- (1) The University shall endeavor to maintain the highest levels of 
academic integrity to encourage original work amongst its students, 
faculty, staff and employees at all levels and the University shall take 
measures to eliminate plagiarism. 

Explanation.- For the purpose of this Ordinances the expression 
‘Plagiarism’ shall mean the passing off of another person’s work as 
one’s own work without acknowledgement of the source, and 
involves copying of phrases, sentences, paragraphs or longer extracts 
from published or unpublished work including from the Internet. 

(2) Modes of Plagiarism: 
The following are considered plagiarism, namely:- 
(a) Turning in someone else's work as your own; 
(b) Copying words or ideas from someone else without giving 
credit; 
(c) Failing to put a quotation in quotation marks; 
(d) Giving incorrect information about the source of a quotation; 
(e) Changing words but copying the sentence structure of a source 
without giving credit; 
(f) Copying so many words or ideas from a source that it makes 
up the majority of your work, whether you give credit or not 
(i.e. not "fair use") 
(3) ‘No-Plagiarism Declaration’ by Students: 
Every student who is required to submit a thesis or dissertation or 
project report or research paper or assignment as part of the 
requirement for award of a Post-Graduate or Doctoral degree shall be 
required to submit a signed statement at the beginning of the Post 
Graduate or Doctor of Philosophy Programme that he is aware of the 
University’s Anti-Plagiarism policy and shall abide by it and he shall 
submit a “No-Plagiarism Declaration” with every thesis or dissertation 
or project report or research paper or assignment submitted by him. 
(4) Responsibility for detecting Plagiarism committed by Students: 
It shall be the primary responsibility of the supervisor or guide or 
teacher to detect the plagiarism, if any, committed by the student 
under his charge, the supervisor or guide or teacher shall run the thesis 
or dissertation or research paper or assignment through the prescribed 
anti-plagiarism detection tool to ensure that it reflects genuine research 
and original work, and he shall furnish a certificate to this effect, a 
supervisor or guide or teacher who fails to put in due diligence to 
detect plagiarism shall be liable for disciplinary action. 
(5) Plagiarism by Employees: 
Teachers and other employees who submit articles or research papers 
or consultancy reports or project reports or who present papers or 
deliver orations in seminars and conferences shall be required to 
uphold the highest ethical standards and not resort to plagiarism and f 
any plagiarism comes to light, they shall be liable for disciplinary 
action. 
(6) Procedure for handling allegations of Plagiarism: 
(i) whenever an allegation of plagiarism is brought to the

(14) Seed Grant Projects: 


The Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya supports newly joined young 
Faculty Members for initiating his/her research at Gati Shakti 
Vishwavidyalaya, with a sum of Rs. 10 Lakhs for Faculty Members 
with background in Science and Technology, and with Rs. 5 Lakhs 
for Faculty Members with background in Management. 

(a) The new Faculty Member shall submit a Seed Grant Proposal 
to Office of Research and Development; 

(b) The Faculty Member shall present the same to a Committee 
consisting of: 

(i) Vice Chancellor; 

(ii) Dean (Academics) 

(iii) Dean (Research & Development) or Faculty-in-Charge 
(Research and Development). 

(c) All Faculty Members, especially those in the domain of the 
proposal, are invited to the presentation; 

(d) If the proposal is accepted in principle, suggestions made by 
the Seed Grant Proposal Review Committee shall be 
incorporated and the revised proposal submitted by the 
Faculty Member to the office of Research and Development, 
on receiving the revised proposal, Faculty-in-Charge 
(Research and Development) may recommend to the Vice 
Chancellor for approval of the Seed Grant; and 

(e) After approval of the Vice Chancellor, a Seed Grant Project 
account shall be opened by the Office of Research and 
Development, clearly stating the budget utilisation under 
different heads such as equipment, consumables and other 
necessary sections, the expenditure towards consumable and 
contingency shall not exceed 25% of the amount granted, no 
furniture items shall be purchased from the seed grant; the 
same shall be provided by the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya. 


(15) Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya Projects: 
Some of activities of the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, such as 
management of hostels, automation, laboratory development, etc. 
are financially regulated Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya Projects, in 
administering such projects, the following points shall be 
considered: 

(a) The Project Investigator of the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya 
Project appointed by the Vice Chancellor, shall seek the 
budget for the financial year from the Grant-in-aid; 

(b) After the budget is approved, a new project account shall be 
opened in the office of Research and Development; 

(c) Any purchase or procurement made under the Gati Shakti 
Vishwavidyalaya Project shall be in accordance with the Gati 
Shakti Vishwavidyalaya norms of expenditure applicable to 
the Grant-in-aid; 

(d) The wages of the hired manpower in Gati Shakti 
Vishwavidyalaya Projects shall follow Gati Shakti 
Vishwavidyalaya norms; 

(e) The Office of Research and Development shall provide to the 
Vice Chancellor quarterly expenditure statement of all Gati

Shakti Vishwavidyalaya Projects duly signed by respective 
Project Investigators; and 

(f) The Project Investigator of the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya 
Project shall seek approval for additional budget for next 
session, before the available fund is exhausted. 


(16) Professional Development Account: 

(a) A Professional Development Account is created for each 
Faculty Member at the time of his joining the Gati Shakti 
Vishwavidyalaya, incomes in Professional Development 
Account are those arising from the academic and professional 
activities of the Faculty Member, the incomes that can be 
credited to this account include: 

(i) part of Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya Overheads from 
Sponsored Research Projects; 

(ii) amount transferred from Consultancy Projects, if any; 

(iii) any other balance income on the project, with the 
approval of Vice Chancellor; 

(b) The amount credited in the Professional Development Account 
can be utilised only for the designated purposes as outlined in 
the extant policy on Professional Development Account; 

(c) The Professional Development Account cannot be operated by 
the Faculty Member, when he is on long leave, short leave, 
leave on “Foreign Service Terms” or on extra-ordinary leave 
and he may be allowed to use the Professional Development 
Account amount, while on sabbatical leave (once the scheme is 
in place). 


(17) Utilization of the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya overhead and 
research and development overhead: 

(a) The Overheads under “Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya 
Development Fund” shall be utilised as per the needs of the Gati 
Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, and with the approval of the Vice 
Chancellor. 

(b) The “Research and Development Overhead” shall be utilised for 
both recurring and non- recurring expenditure, including 
compensation of the project staff, honorarium to regular staff 
members, travel and other expenditures approval by the Vice 
Chancellor.

sponsored Research Projects, Consultancy Projects and other

56. Schedule of financial General Principles of delegation of powers or Delegation of 
elcid financial powers:- 

(1) Any official of the University shall not incur any expenditure 
or enter into any liability involving expenditure unless the 
approval for the same has been taken from the Competent 
Authority of the University. 

(2) In case where it becomes necessary to issue a sanction to 
expenditure before funds or grants are released, the sanction 
shall specify that such expenditure is subject to funds or grants 
being disbursed. 

(3) Lapse of Sanction: A sanction for any expenditure, unless it is 
specifically renewed, shall lapse within a period of twelve 
months from the date of issue of such sanction provided that: 

(a) When the period of sanction is prescribed in the sanction 
itself, it shall lapse on the expiry of such period; 

(b) When there is a specific provision in a sanction that the 
expenditure shall be met from budget provision of 
specified financial year then the sanction shall lapse at 
the end of financial year. 

(4) Unless otherwise specified, all delegations are on per occasion 
basis, in order to get the approval of higher Competent 
Authority, splitting shall be avoided and discouraged. 

(5) Delegated powers may be delegated further without prior 
approval of the authority that originally delegated the powers. 

(6) All the power delegated hereunder are subject to budget 
allocation under the relevant budget-head and after following 
the prescribed procedure and guidelines indicated in the Act or 
Statutes issued from time to time by Government of India or 
Executive Council. 

(7) In case of ambiguity or conflicts between the provisions 
stipulated in this handbook and in the original source such as 
General Finance Rules, etc. or the prevailing rules or 
guidelines or law of Government of India, the provisions 
contained in the original source Government of India rules shall 
prevail. 

(8) All purchase proposals shall be processed as per the procedure 
prescribed in the General Finance Rules, purchase procedures, 
all Authorities concerned shall submit the proposals to the 
Vice- Chancellor OR Registrar for administrative approval. 

(9) For cases other than Works: All cases of expenditure shall be 
concurred by Finance. 

(10) A formal sanction for creation of posts or incurring of 
expenditure shall be communicated to all concerned, indicating

(11) Notwithstanding these delegations, in cases where adequate 
competition does not exist or emergent purchases are to be 
made, expenditure is to be incurred in relaxation of the 
prescribed procedure, approval of the Vice-Chancellor with the 
concurrence of Finance shall be necessary. 

(12) Notwithstanding these delegation of Financial Powers, Vice 
Chancellor can exercise powers of any of the officers to whom 
the power has been delegated. 

(13) The constitution of the Committee for procurement shall be done 
by the Registrar OR Vice Chancellor as per the delegated 
powers.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 24th June, 2026 


S.O. 3387(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH |46B in the 
stretch of land from Km. 0 to Km. |7 (SDO Khategaon) in the district of DEWAS in the state of MADHYA PRADESH, 
hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this notification in 
the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(l) of section 3C of the 
said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, SDO Khategaon in writing and shall set out 
the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person 
or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the 
Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be inspected by 
the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

5.0. 347(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by section |6 read with sub-section (3) of section 25 of 
the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 206 ([] of 206), the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary so 
to do in the public interest and after consulting the Bureau, hereby makes the following Order, namely: — 


I. Short title and commencement. - () This Order may be called the Transition Facilitation (Quality Control) Order, 
2026. 


(2) It shall come into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application. - This Order shall apply to the goods or articles covered under the Quality Control Orders specified in 
the Schedule appended to this Order. 


3. Compulsory use of standard mark.- () Notwithstanding anything contained in the Quality Control Orders specified 
in the Schedule, goods or articles covered thereunder shall conform to the corresponding Indian Standards and shall be 
permitted use of a Standard Mark under a license from Bureau of Indian Standards as per Scheme II of the Schedule II 
to the Bureau of Indian Standards (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 208, subject to the provisions of this Order. 


(2) The license under sub-clause () shall be available only to a manufacturer for supplying to the person who has been 
granted specific permission under clause 4 of this Order. 


(3) The person granted permission shall ensure that the goods or articles permitted under this Order conform to the 
applicable Indian Standards prescribed under the corresponding Quality Control Orders. 


(4) The Bureau of Indian Standards, in consultation with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, 
shall either directly or through agencies notified by it, carry out market surveillance of such goods to verify continued 
conformance with the applicable Indian Standards. 


4. Grant of permission. - () Permission under this Order may be granted by the Department for Promotion of Industry 
and Internal Trade, - 


(a) to a person that is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 20l3; and 
(b) based on the risk assessment of the person by an Implementation Committee constituted under the Order. 
(2) The permission granted under sub-clause () shall be subject to such conditions as may be specified therein. 


(3) There shall be an Implementation Committee for the purposes of this Order, and the said Committee shall consist 
of- 


(a) Additional Secretary or Joint Secretary (I/c Technical Regulations), Department for Promotion of Industry and 
Internal Trade-Chairperson; 


(b) Additional Secretary or Joint Secretary, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade of the concerned 
Product- Member;

(c) Joint Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs -Member; 

(d) Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce - Member; 

(e) Representative of Directorate General of Foreign Trade (not below the rank of Joint Secretary level) --Member; 
(f) Representative of Bureau of Indian Standards (not below the rank of Joint Secretary level)-Member; 


(g) Director or Deputy Secretary or equivalent (I/c Technical Regulations), Department for Promotion of Industry and 
Internal Trade- Convenor; and 


(h) Any other representative not below the rank of Deputy Secretary or Director from other Ministry or Department or 
Organization invited by the Chairperson; 


(4) The Implementation Committee shall assess the person based on its technical capability, demonstrated experience; 
manner of ensuring quality assurance across its supply chain including through control over its design and 
manufacturing; history of conduct and compliance integrity; and its commitment to establish supply chain capabilities 
in India for the concerned goods and articles by promoting technological adoption/advancement or design capabilities 
or research and development; or its compliance for the concerned Quality Control Order for a continuous period of 
three years without any default; and any other relevant factors. 


(5) The Implementation Committee may interact with the person and rely upon documents, declarations, certifications, 
undertakings, independent assessments, as may be provided by the person, and such other material that it considers 
appropriate for the purpose of its assessment. 


(6) In case of breach of conditions, misrepresentation of material facts or failure of product to conform to applicable 
Indian standards, the Central Government may suspend, modify or withdraw any permission granted under this Order, 
after giving opportunity to be heard. 


5. Application and other modalities. - (.) The applications for permission under the Order shall be accepted within 
twenty-four months from the date of commencement of this Order. 


(2) All relevant details pertaining to this Order in respect of the application process, documentation required, 
entitlements, monitoring and compliance, etc., shall be specified in guidelines issued by the Department for Promotion 
of Industry and Internal Trade and be available at the website (https://www.dpiit.gov.in). 


6. Duration and savings. -(l) This Order shall remain in force for a period of five years from the date of its 
commencement and shall thereafter stand rescinded unless it is extended by the Central Government by notification in 
the Official Gazette. 


(2) Notwithstanding such rescission, any permission granted under this Order prior to the date of rescission shall 
continue to remain valid for the period specified therein unless suspended, modified or withdrawn in accordance with 
the provisions of this Order. 


(3) The rescission of this Order shall not affect any right, obligation, liability, investigation, proceeding or action arising 
under this Order prior to such rescission. 


7. Interpretation. - If any question arises relating to the interpretation of this Order, the same shall be referred to the 
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade for its decision.

और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 2032(E) तारीख 22/04/2026, जो भारत के राजपत्र, असाधारण, 
भाग Il, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (ii) F प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा महाराष्ट्र राज्य के पुणे जिले में NHGO के कि.मी. 72.9 से 
कि.मी. 42 तक के राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग के निर्माण (चोड़ाकरने / चार लेन का बनाने, आदि), अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन और प्रचालन के

और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन तारीख 3/05/2026 को 
“थे इंडियन एक्सप्रेस [इंग्लिश]! , 73/05/2026 को “लोकमत (मराठी +)” दोनों में प्रकाशित किया गया था ; 


जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और उसका 
उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (॥) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 24th June, 2026 


5.0. 3388(E).—Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 452(E) Dated:9/03/2026 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (.) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for construction of Toll Plaza Maintenance, management and operation of NH-l68G 
in the stretch of land from Km. 0 to Km. 7.5 in the district of MAHESANA in the state of GUJARAT 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “The Times of India” dated 
28/03/2026, “Divya Bhaskar” dated 26/03/2026; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 24th June, 2026 


S.O. 3396(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 526(E) Dated:03/02/2026, 1137(E) Dated:03/03/2026 , published in the Gazette of India, 
Extraordinary, Part I, Section 3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to 
acquire the land specified in the Schedule annexed to the said notification for construction (widening/two lane with 
paved shoulder/four laning etc.), Maintenance, management and operation of NH135B in the stretch of land from 
Km. 36+700 to Km. 73+813 in the district of REWA in the state of MADHYA PRADESH 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “Star Samachar Satna” dated 
21/02/2026 , “Dainik Wipra Express Daily Rewa” dated 21/02/2026 , “Vindhya Bharat Daily Rewa” dated 
18/03/2026 , “Dainik Jagran Daily Rewa” dated 18/03/2026 ; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

S.O. 3427(E).—In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National 
Highways Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being 
satisfied that for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required 
for building (widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of 
Chittorgarh Bypass connecting NH-27 to NH-48 in the stretch of land from Km. 0.000 to Km. 8.140 (District 
Collectorate Office Chittorgarh) in the district of Chittorgarh in the state of RAJASTHAN, hereby declares its 
intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Addl Dist Collector (A) Chittorgarh 
in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of 
being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making 
such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either

allow or disallow the objections. Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 
3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

“मिश्रधातु अथवा गैर-मिश्रधातु इस्पात के हॉट ties फ्लैट उत्पादों” (जिन्हें इसके बाद “विचाराधीन उत्पाद” 
अथवा “संबद्ध वस्तु” कहा गया है) के आयातों के संबंध में पाटनरोधी जांच शुरू करने हेतु आवेदन दायर किया है। 


आवेदकों ने आरोप लगाया है कि विचाराधीन उत्पाद का आयात संबद्ध देशों से पाटित कीमतों पर किया जा रहा 
है, जिससे घरेलू उद्योग को महत्वपूर्ण क्षति हो रही है। आवेदकों ने यह भी आरोप लगाया है कि पाटित आयातों के 
कारण घरेलू उद्योग को आगे और महत्वपूर्ण क्षति होने का खतरा विद्यमान है तथा उन्होंने संबद्ध देशों से 
विचाराधीन उत्पाद के आयातों पर पाटनरोधी शुल्क लगाए जाने का अनुरोध किया है। 


विचाराधीन उत्पाद 


वर्तमान जांच में विचाराधीन उत्पाद (“पीयूसी”) “मिश्रधातु अथवा गैर-मिश्रधातु इस्पात के हॉट ties फ्लैट 
उत्पाद, जो RIS, प्लेटेड अथवा कोटेड न हों तथा जिनकी मोटाई 25 मिमी तक और चौड़ाई 2400 मिमी तक 
हो” है। 

विचाराधीन उत्पाद में ऐसे उत्पाद शामिल हैं जो हॉट-रोलिंग से आगे संसाधित नहीं किए गए हैं तथा मिश्रधातु 
अथवा गैर-मिश्रधातु इस्पात के फ्लैट उत्पाद हैं, चाहे वे प्राइम अथवा नॉन-प्राइम स्थिति में हों और जिनके किनारे 
“एज़-रोल्ड”, “fers”, “स्लिट”, “fies”, “शीयर्ड”, “लेज़र-कट”, “गैस-कट” अथवा किसी अन्य प्रकार के हों। ये 
उत्पाद Peace अथवा नॉन-पिकल्ड (स्किन-पास अथवा टेम्पर्रिंग सहित या बिना), fae अथवा नॉन-स्लिट, 
नॉर्मलाइज़्ड अथवा अननॉर्मलाइज़्ड, अल्ट्रासोनिक परीक्षणयुक्त अथवा परीक्षणरहित, ऑयल्ड अथवा नॉन-ऑयल्ड 
हो सकते हैं। ये उत्पाद “एज़-रोल्ड”, “थर्मो-मैकेनिकल ties”, “थर्मो-मैकेनिकल कंट्रोल्ड Cee”, “Hates Tes”, 
“नॉर्मलाइज़्ड रोल्ड”, “नॉर्मलाइज़्ड” अथवा अन्य समान प्रक्रियाओं से गुजरे हो सकते हैं। इन उत्पादों पर पिकलिंग, 
ऑयलिंग, रीवाइंडिंग, रीकॉइलिंग, टेम्पर रोलिंग, हीट ट्रीटमेंट आदि जैसी विभिन्न प्रसंस्करण प्रक्रियाएं भी की गई 
हो सकती हैं। ये उत्पाद सैंड ब्लास्टेड, शॉट ब्लास्टेड अथवा इसी प्रकार की अन्य प्रक्रियाओं से भी गुजरे हो सकते 
हैं। विचाराधीन उत्पाद में कॉयल रूप में तथा कट-टू-लेंथ रूप में उपलब्ध हॉट Ces फ्लैट उत्पाद शामिल हैं। 


निम्नलिखित विचाराधीन उत्पाद का उपयोग ऑटोमोबाइल, तेल एवं गैस पाइपलाइन/अन्वेषण, कोल्ड Us 
इस्पात उत्पादों, पाइप निर्माण, सामान्य इंजीनियरिंग एवं फैब्रिकेशन, निर्माण क्षेत्र, पूंजीगत वस्तुओं, सीमेंट, 
उर्वरक एवं रिफाइनरी उद्योगों के प्रक्रिया उपकरणों, अर्थ-मूरविंग उपकरणों आदि में किया जाता है। 

विचाराधीन उत्पाद को सीमा शुल्क टैरिफ शीर्षकों 7208, 7244, 7225 तथा 7226 के अंतर्गत वर्गीकृत किया 


गया है। सीमा शुल्क वर्गीकरण केवल संकेतात्मक है तथा वर्तमान जांच में विचाराधीन उत्पाद के दायरे पर किसी 
प्रकार से बाध्यकारी नहीं है। 


विचाराधीन उत्पाद में स्टेनलेस स्टील के हॉट Ces फ्लैट उत्पाद शामिल नहीं हैं। 

आवेदकों ने निम्नलिखित उत्पाद नियंत्रण संख्या (पीसीएन) प्रस्तावित की है, जिसे वियतनाम के मूल के अथवा 
वहां से निर्यातित “मिश्रधातु अथवा गैर-मिश्रधातु इस्पात के हॉट रोल्ड फ्लैट उत्पादों” के आयातों से संबंधित 
पाटनरोधी जांच, मामला सं. Wet (ATaATE)-73/2024 में अपनाया गया था, जिसके अंतिम जांच परिणाम दिनांक 
43 अगस्त, 2025 को जारी किए गए थे।

समान वस्तु 


घरेलू उद्योग द्वारा उत्पादित संबद्ध वस्तुओं और संबद्ध देशों से आयातित विचाराधीन उत्पाद के बीच कोई ज्ञात 
अंतर नहीं है। घरेलू उद्योग द्वारा उत्पादित संबद्ध वस्तुएं और संबद्ध देशों से आयातित विचाराधीन उत्पाद भौतिक 
एवं रासायनिक विशेषताओं, निर्माण प्रक्रिया एवं तकनीक, कार्यों एवं उपयोगों, उत्पाद विनिर्देशों, मूल्य निर्धारण, 
वितरण एवं विपणन तथा टैरिफ वर्गीकरण सहित सभी दृष्टियों से तुलनीय हैं। दोनों उत्पाद तकनीकी एवं 
वाणिज्यिक दृष्टि से एक-दूसरे के स्थान पर उपयोग किए जा सकते हैं तथा उपभोक्ता उनका परस्पर विनिमेय रूप 
से उपयोग करते हैं। अतः वर्तमान जांच के प्रयोजन हेतु घरेलू उद्योग द्वारा उत्पादित संबद्ध वस्तुओं को संबद्ध देशों 
से आयातित विचाराधीन उत्पाद के “समान वस्तु” के रूप में माना गया है। 


घरेलू उद्योग और स्थिति 


यह आवेदन मैसर्स जेएसडब्ल्यू स्टील लिमिटेड, जेएसडब्ल्यू विजयनगर मेटालिक्स लिमिटेड तथा जिंदल स्टील 
ओडिशा लिमिटेड द्वारा दायर किया गया है। आवेदकों ने जांच अवधि के दौरान संबद्ध देशों से संबद्ध वस्तुओं का 
आयात नहीं किया है। इसके अतिरिक्त, आवेदक संबद्ध देशों में संबद्ध वस्तुओं के किसी निर्यातक अथवा भारत में 
किसी आयातक से संबंधित नहीं हैं। इस आवेदन का समर्थन टाटा स्टील लिमिटेड तथा स्टील अथॉरिटी ऑफ 
इंडिया लिमिटेड द्वारा किया गया है। 


आवेदकों ने प्रस्तुत किया है कि समर्थनकर्ता के अतिरिक्त भारत में संबद्ध वस्तुओं का एक अन्य उत्पादक 
आर्सेलरमित्तल निष्पॉन स्टील इंडिया लिमिटेड (“एएमएनएस”) है, जिसकी जापान में एक संबद्ध इकाई निष्पॉन 
स्टील कॉरपोरेशन है, जो संबद्ध वस्तुओं का उत्पादक/निर्यातक है। एएमएनएस ने क्षति जांच अवधि के दौरान 
निष्पॉन स्टील से संबद्ध वस्तुओं का आयात किया Sl तदनुसार, प्राधिकारी ने नियमावली के नियम 2(ख) के 
अंतर्गत एएमएनएस को घरेलू उद्योग का भाग माने जाने हेतु अयोग्य माना है। 


अभिलेख पर उपलब्ध साक्ष्यों के अनुसार, प्राधिकारी ने नोट किया है कि आवेदक तथा समर्थनकर्ता मिलकर जांच 
अवधि के दौरान भारत में समान वस्तु के कुल उत्पादन का एक प्रमुख भाग प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं। अतः प्राधिकारी 
ने पाटनरोधी नियमावली के नियम 2(ख) के प्रावधानों के अंतर्गत आवेदकों को घरेलू उद्योग माना है। इसके 
अतिरिक्त, यह आवेदन पाटनरोधी नियमावली के नियम 5(3) की आवश्यकताओं को भी पूरा करता है।

क्षति हुई है। आवेदकों ने दावा किया है कि क्षति जांच अवधि के दौरान आयातों की मात्रा में निरपेक्ष रूप से तथा

इन आयातों के कारण घरेलू उद्योग की कीमतों पर दबाव और गिरावट आई है। बिक्री में वृद्धि के बावजूद घरेलू

BASIS OF ALLEGED DUMPING 
Normal Value for China PR 


The applicants have claimed that China PR should be treated as a non-market economy and the 
producers from China PR should be directed to demonstrate that market economy conditions 
prevail in the industry with regard to production and sales of the subject goods. Unless the Chinese 
producers show that market economy conditions prevail, their normal value should be determined 
in terms of Paragraph 7 of Annexure-I to the Rules. 


Applicants have claimed that import price from Korea RP (market economy third country) is 
appropriate for determination of normal value for China PR because Korea RP is the largest 
exporting country of subject goods to India and it is a market economy country. 


Therefore, for purpose of the present investigation, normal value for China PR has been determined 
considering import prices of subject goods from Korea RP into India after adjustment of ocean 
freight, insurance, inland transportation, port and handling charges, commission and bank charges. 
The claim of the Applicants may further be examined during the course of the investigation after 
receiving comments from all interested parties. For the purpose of initiation, the normal value for 
China PR has been determined based on the methodology proposed by the Applicants. 


Normal Value for Japan and Russia 


The Applicants have claimed normal value for Japan and Russia based on the prices prevailing in 
the domestic market in Japan and Russia. The Applicants have provided information based on 
information reported in BigMint and Platts report. 


The Authority has accepted the claim of the applicants in respect of the determination of normal 
value for the subject countries for the purpose of initiation of this investigation. 


Export Price 


The export price of the subject goods has been determined by considering CIF price of the subject 
goods, as reported in the DGCI&S data. Adjustments on account of ocean freight, marine 
insurance, commission, bank charges, port expenses, inland freight and credit cost have been made. 


Dumping Margin 


The normal value and the export price have been compared at ex-factory level, which prima facie 
shows that the dumping margin is above the de-minimis level and is significant with respect to the 
product under consideration exported from the subject countries. Thus, there is sufficient prima 
facie evidence that the product under consideration from subject countries is being dumped in the 
Indian market by the exporters from the subject countries.

The Applicants have requested for retrospective imposition of the anti-dumping duty on imports of

a. There is a history of dumping in India as is evident from the fact of past investigations on

b. The importer should have been aware of dumping by the present subject countries, based 
on its experience from past investigations which established the price levels at which

c. Non imposition of duty is likely to lead to a rise in dumping from subject countries. The

INITIATION OF ANTI-DUMPING INVESTIGATION 


On the basis of the duly substantiated application filed by the applicants, and having satisfied itself,
